=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents against the buyer's interests. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Positions (SPA-N-001 to SPA-N-016)

**Preliminary notes**
- The Seller's cover note says these positions were "settled at principal level" and are "not intended to be re-opened." Nothing in the Seller's draft binds Wattlebridge. Before accepting any "settled" position, the deal team should check it against its own written record of principal-level agreement.
- The Seller's market claims (10–20% caps, ~1% baskets, 12–18 month limitation periods) are unsupported in the material. They should be tested against precedent before being relied on.
- I have the Seller's summary of clauses, not the full SPA. Clause references below follow the Seller's numbering and should be checked against the mark-up.
- Items marked for Australian counsel confirmation (fraud, non-reliance, sandbagging, privacy) turn on NSW and Commonwealth law and should be verified by Australian counsel before the mark-up goes out.

---

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller position:** Aggregate general warranty liability capped at 20% of price (AUD 4,800,000).
- **Buyer wants:** Open at a higher general cap (around 50%), with a fallback of around 30%. Fundamental, tax and specific indemnity claims sit outside the general cap, up to 100% of price.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 50% general, 100% for fundamental, tax and specific indemnities. *Reason: A 20% cap leaves the buyer bearing most of the loss on a material warranty breach, while the known exposures are excluded from the regime altogether.*

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket
- **Seller position:** De minimis AUD 25,000. Basket AUD 250,000 (about 1.04% of price), with only the excess above the basket recoverable (deductible structure).
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis around AUD 10,000, with related claims aggregated. A tipping (first-dollar) basket of around AUD 120,000 (0.5%), so that once it is passed, the whole claim is recoverable. No threshold for fundamental, tax or specific indemnity claims.
- **Recommendation:** Counter with AUD 10,000 de minimis and a AUD 120,000 tipping basket. *Reason: A deductible basket of about 1% can absorb most claims on a business of this size.*

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller position:** General warranty claims notified within 18 months of Completion. One limitation period applies to all claims.
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months for general warranties. Tax claims run to 60 days after the relevant statutory assessment period ends. Fundamental and fraud claims run for 6 years, aligned with the NSW contract limitation period.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 24 months for general warranties. *Reason: 18 months from a late-2026 Completion expires before FY27 income tax returns are lodged and assessed, so problems in that year could go undetected.*

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental and title regime
- **Seller position:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties, "for administrative simplicity."
- **Buyer wants:** Fundamental warranties (title to shares, no encumbrances, capacity, authority) outside the general cap, with no de minimis or basket, a cap of up to 100% of price, and a 6-year claims period.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. *Reason: Title defects go to what the buyer is actually acquiring, so they cannot sensibly be subject to a general cap and a 18-month window.*

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller position:** No fraud carve-out. The limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to "all Claims of any nature," which read literally includes fraud.
- **Buyer wants:** An express carve-out for fraud, dishonest concealment and wilful misconduct from the caps, time limits, disclosure, non-reliance, buyer-knowledge and exclusive-remedy provisions. (For Australian counsel: confirm the extent to which non-reliance wording can exclude misleading-conduct liability under the Australian Consumer Law.)
- **Recommendation:** Insert an express fraud carve-out. *Reason: As drafted, the limitations purport to cover fraud, which is likely unenforceable in part and invites dispute.*

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller position:** General disclosure of the entire data room (as at 5.00pm, 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and public records. Expressed to be "without limiting" specific disclosures.
- **Buyer wants:** Reject general disclosure. Disclosure only against specific warranties, fairly disclosed with reasonable particularity and referring to the specific document. Public records disclosed only through searches the buyer has specifically listed.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. *Reason: Deeming the whole data room disclosed would hollow out every warranty, including those covering matters the Seller has already flagged as open.*

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller position (cl 8.3):** No claim for any matter the buyer or its advisers knew of, including anything "discoverable from the data room or public records."
- **Buyer wants:** Delete. Insert an express pro-sandbagging clause, so that the buyer's rights are unaffected by its knowledge. (For Australian counsel: the default position on sandbagging is not settled in the buyer's favour, so express wording is needed.) Known issues are addressed through specific indemnities and conditions, not through warranty claims.
- **Recommendation:** Delete and replace with an express pro-sandbagging clause. *Reason: "Discoverable from the data room" would bar warranty claims on every issue the Seller has disclosed in its letter.*

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller position:** The Seller will use reasonable endeavours. Consent is treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. DD-002 records about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue (around 30%). The disclosure confirms no final written consent and no evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are met.
- **Buyer wants:** Completion condition precedent: written, unconditional Bluefen consent, with the clause 11.3 conditions satisfied or waived by the buyer alone. No deemed satisfaction on "delivery." If the buyer waives the condition, a price adjustment or escrow tied to Bluefen revenue. A termination right if consent is not obtained by a long-stop date. A specific indemnity for loss of the Bluefen relationship caused by consent failure. (Confirm that the share sale triggers clause 11.2.)
- **Recommendation:** Make it a condition precedent with a buyer-only waiver. *Reason: Losing around 30% of revenue is a value event that a warranty claim cannot adequately compensate.*

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller position:** About AUD 3.2m outstanding. Not repaid. Release to be provided after Completion. No discharge of security included.
- **Buyer wants:** On a debt-free, cash-free basis, the Riverlark debt is repaid at Completion from the price, under a payoff letter, with all security (including PPSR registrations and any guarantees) discharged at the same time. The funds flow must show it. Any change-of-control consent under cl 8.1 obtained. If repayment cannot happen at Completion, the buyer withholds funds until the discharge is delivered.
- **Recommendation:** Require payoff and discharge at Completion, deducted from price. *Reason: Leaving AUD 3.2m outstanding after Completion means the buyer effectively pays for the debt twice, or becomes the debtor.*

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller position:** Conditional Completion bonuses of AUD 420,000 (DD-005). Not in the draft funds flow. Described as "a matter for the Seller."
- **Buyer wants:** The Seller bears all Completion bonuses and related on-costs (NSW payroll tax, superannuation guarantee at 12%, and any other employer costs). These are included in the funds flow as transaction costs or debt-like items and deducted from price. A specific indemnity for any employee claims relating to the bonuses. Confirm whether the continued-employment conditions create post-Completion retention costs for the buyer.
- **Recommendation:** Treat as a Seller cost, deducted in the funds flow. *Reason: Payments triggered by the sale are transaction costs and should not fall on the buyer after Completion.*

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller position:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment. Considered "adequate."
- **Buyer wants:** Reject the position. (a) The Seller pays the AUD 180,000 open SOW3 balance before Completion, or it is deducted from price, with bank evidence (DD-010 is a record, not verification of non-payment). (b) A confirmatory written assignment of all SOW3 Project Materials from Ironquay as a condition precedent (per DD-004 cl 7.3). (c) A specific indemnity covering any third-party claim to IP in Company products derived from Ironquay work, outside the basket, with a cap of up to 100% of price and a 6-year claims period. (d) IP ownership warranties treated as fundamental.
- **Recommendation:** Require the condition precedent and a full IP indemnity. *Reason: The indemnity covers a fee, not the ownership risk the buyer is actually taking on.*

### SPA-N-012: Export and privacy incident (DD-006)
- **Seller position:** Preliminary operational matter, "not expected to be material." No loss amount stated.
- **Buyer wants:** Reject the materiality characterisation. Before signing: forensic investigation of the scope (access logs, whether the link was opened, by whom); a data inventory for the roughly 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps); an assessment under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) Notifiable Data Breaches scheme, including whether there is an eligible data breach; and a check of customer contract notification obligations. Confirm whether the Company is an APP entity (the implied revenue of around AUD 12m suggests the small business exemption is unlikely to apply). Specific indemnity covering notification, regulatory, remediation and third-party costs, outside the basket. Completion conditional on a satisfactory investigation outcome, with a retention or escrow until it is resolved.
- **Recommendation:** Complete the investigation before signing and take a specific indemnity. *Reason: The Seller cannot say whether notification is required or what the scope is, so the buyer cannot price the exposure.*

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller position:** Three renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 total). Described as ordinary course.
- **Buyer wants:** A schedule of all three contracts showing terms, renewal dates, whether any renewal straddles Completion, termination rights, change-of-control triggers and any prepayment. Treat multi-year or prepaid amounts, and any amounts attributable to pre-Completion periods, as debt-like items. Assess the three together, not as separate sub-threshold items. A warranty that the renewals are in the ordinary course on arm's-length terms.
- **Recommendation:** Aggregate, schedule and treat prepaid or out-of-period amounts as debt-like. *Reason: The disclosure does not say whether the renewals are terminable or accrued, so the "ordinary course" label is unverified.*

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller position:** A single regime for all claims, applying the same cap, basket, time limit and exclusive remedy.
- **Buyer wants:** Separate categories with different terms:
  1. General warranties: general cap, basket, 24 months.
  2. Fundamental (title, capacity, authority): outside the cap, no basket, 6 years, cap up to price.
  3. Tax: indemnity with no basket, time running to statutory limit plus 60 days, cap up to price.
  4. IP ownership and privacy: specific indemnities outside the general regime.
  5. Known matters (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, bonuses, privacy, Sandbar, lease and Mossvale consents): first-dollar, outside the basket, not subject to the buyer-knowledge qualifier.
  6. Fraud: uncapped.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the single regime. *Reason: Under a 20% cap applying to everything, a title defect is capped at AUD 4.8m, and a tax assessment faces the same basket as a minor warranty breach.*

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller position:** Title evidenced by the share register at DD-012, showing Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of issued shares.
- **Buyer wants:** The register is a starting point, not proof of title. Required: a current ASIC company extract; a register of members certified by the company secretary; confirmation that there are no other share classes, options or convertible instruments; a PPSR search over the shares; a warranty that the Seller is sole legal and beneficial owner, free of encumbrances; board approval and executed transfer documents; and confirmation that stamp duty on the transfer (generally the purchaser's cost in NSW) is budgeted.
- **Recommendation:** Complete independent verification before signing. *Reason: The register shows the Seller's version of title, not that no third party holds a competing interest.*

### SPA-N-016: Tax and IP open terms
- **Seller position:** Tax and IP warranties are "settled under the general regime," meaning the 20% cap, basket and 18-month period.
- **Buyer wants:** Tax: a pre-Completion tax indemnity (covering income tax, GST, PAYG withholding, payroll tax and any other pre-Completion liabilities), outside the basket and cap (up to price), with a claims period running to 60 days after the statutory assessment period ends. Standalone tax warranties, including GST registration and compliance. IP: full warranties on ownership of core IP, non-infringement, open-source compliance for the SaaS platform, and employee and contractor IP assignments. Ownership warranties treated as fundamental. Infringement warranties scheduled and general.
- **Recommendation:** Take the tax indemnity outside the general regime. *Reason: Tax exposures crystallise on ATO assessment, often long after 18 months, and should not be capped by a general warranty regime.*

---

## Summary and next steps

**Pre-signing priorities (in order):**
1. **Bluefen (SPA-N-008):** Make consent a condition precedent with a buyer-only waiver.
2. **Riverlark (SPA-N-009):** Payoff and discharge at Completion, deducted from price.
3. **Privacy incident (SPA-N-012):** Complete the forensic and NDB assessment before signing.
4. **Ironquay (SPA-N-011):** Pay or deduct the AUD 180,000 balance and obtain the confirmatory assignment.
5. **Bonuses (SPA-N-010):** Correct the funds flow to include the AUD 420,000 and related on-costs.
6. **Structural points (SPA-N-005, 006, 007, 014):** Fraud carve-out, rejection of general data-room disclosure, deletion of the buyer-knowledge qualifier, and separate claim categories. These are non-negotiable in substance, since the current draft would leave most known issues without remedy.

**Known quantified exposures (excluding Bluefen revenue and the privacy matter):** AUD 3.2m Riverlark + AUD 420k bonuses + AUD 330k Sandbar + AUD 180k Ironquay = **about AUD 4.13m**. These should be dealt with through price deduction or specific indemnity, not through the general warranty regime.

**Verification required:** Independent confirmation of the Ironquay payment status, the Sandbar contract terms, the Mossvale and landlord consent requirements, the Bluefen clause 11.3 conditions, and the ASIC and PPSR title searches.

Before signing: forensic investigation of the scope (access logs, whether the link was opened, by whom); a data inventory for the roughly 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps); an assessment under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) Notifiable Data Breaches scheme, including whether there is an eligible data breach; and a check of customer contract notification obligations. Confirm whether the Company is an APP entity (the implied revenue of around AUD 12m suggests the small business exemption is unlikely to apply). Specific indemnity covering notification, regulatory, remediation and third-party costs, outside the basket. Completion conditional on a satisfactory investigation outcome, with a retention or escrow until it is resolved.
- **Recommendation:** Complete the investigation before signing and take a specific indemnity. *Reason: The Seller cannot say whether notification is required or what the scope is, so the buyer cannot price the exposure.*

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller position:** Three renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 total). Described as ordinary course.
- **Buyer wants:** A schedule of all three contracts showing terms, renewal dates, whether any renewal straddles Completion, termination rights, change-of-control triggers and any prepayment. Treat multi-year or prepaid amounts, and any amounts attributable to pre-Completion periods, as debt-like items. Assess the three together, not as separate sub-threshold items. A warranty that the renewals are in the ordinary course on arm's-length terms.
- **Recommendation:** Aggregate, schedule and treat prepaid or out-of-period amounts as debt-like. *Reason: The disclosure does not say whether the renewals are terminable or accrued, so the "ordinary course" label is unverified.*

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller position:** A single regime for all claims, applying the same cap, basket, time limit and exclusive remedy.
- **Buyer wants:** Separate categories with different terms:
  1. General warranties: general cap, basket, 24 months.
  2. Fundamental (title, capacity, authority): outside the cap, no basket, 6 years, cap up to price.
  3. Tax: indemnity with no basket, time running to statutory limit plus 60 days, cap up to price.
  4. IP ownership and privacy: specific indemnities outside the general regime.
  5. Known matters (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, bonuses, privacy, Sandbar, lease and Mossvale consents): first-dollar, outside the basket, not subject to the buyer-knowledge qualifier.
  6. Fraud: uncapped.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the single regime. *Reason: Under a 20% cap applying to everything, a title defect is capped at AUD 4.8m, and a tax assessment faces the same basket as a minor warranty breach.*

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller position:** Title evidenced by the share register at DD-012, showing Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of issued shares.
- **Buyer wants:** The register is a starting point, not proof of title. Required: a current ASIC company extract; a register of members certified by the company secretary; confirmation that there are no other share classes, options or convertible instruments; a PPSR search over the shares; a warranty that the Seller is sole legal and beneficial owner, free of encumbrances; board approval and executed transfer documents; and confirmation that stamp duty on the transfer (generally the purchaser's cost in NSW) is budgeted.
- **Recommendation:** Complete independent verification before signing. *Reason: The register shows the Seller's version of title, not that no third party holds a competing interest.*

### SPA-N-016: Tax and IP open terms
- **Seller position:** Tax and IP warranties are "settled under the general regime," meaning the 20% cap, basket and 18-month period.
- **Buyer wants:** Tax: a pre-Completion tax indemnity (covering income tax, GST, PAYG withholding, payroll tax and any other pre-Completion liabilities), outside the basket and cap (up to price), with a claims period running to 60 days after the statutory assessment period ends. Standalone tax warranties, including GST registration and compliance. IP: full warranties on ownership of core IP, non-infringement, open-source compliance for the SaaS platform, and employee and contractor IP assignments. Ownership warranties treated as fundamental. Infringement warranties scheduled and general.
- **Recommendation:** Take the tax indemnity outside the general regime. *Reason: Tax exposures crystallise on ATO assessment, often long after 18 months, and should not be capped by a general warranty regime.*
